pr_title: Fix mqtt sensor or binary_sensor state not saved after expiry
pr_body:

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
An mqtt `sensor` or `binary_sensor` should save the state if after expiry of the first payload the same payload arrives. The expiry triggers so save the state, so at any value received the state should be updated if after expire a new value is received, even if the value is the same.

This bug is a regression on #100438. This issue is fixed by tracking if the sensor 's expiry state was changed.

I am seeing this same problem on 2023.10.0 and 2023.10.1. It appears that if a MQTT binary sensor becomes unavailable it sticks. Even when new states become available, it continues to show as unavailable in Home Assistant.

If I subscribe to MQTT topics in the Home Assistant UI (or via any other method) I can see the new states being published as expected.

This is most noticable when receiving somewhat unreliable data, e.g. wireless sensors. In my specific case, I'm using [mqtt4hasd](https://piglab.reaperlegion.net/home-automation/hass/mqtt4hass)+rtl_433, which does not explicitly publish available/unavailable status, but does publish a `expire_after` with the config, and previously Home Assistant would correctly handle that.

Edit: this also affects other MQTT sensor types. It appears that if a value expires, it stays offline until a _different_ state is received, where in 2023.09 and older, any state would restore the sensor to available.
Can you see the messages coming in when you subscribe to the topic using the debug functions on the MQTT config page?
The logs that are interesting are that of HA Core. It helps to set the log level to `debug`.

> This is most noticable when receiving somewhat unreliable data, e.g. wireless sensors. In my specific case, I'm using [mqtt4hasd](https://piglab.reaperlegion.net/home-automation/hass/mqtt4hass)+rtl_433, which does not explicitly publish available/unavailable status, but does publish a `expire_after` with the config, and previously Home Assistant would correctly handle that.

That should not be a problem. There is one thing though. Because the value is not changing, the state is not updated.
May be you can set the `force_update` option to `True`.

I'll have a look at the behaviour of `expire_after` here. It may be a bug that the timer is not reset when a payload comes in.
I can confirm this is an issue with MQTT. A message is received but because the state is not changed is is not reset by the timer, it does not work.
See linked PR for a fix. Setting `force_update` to `True` will also fix the issue in your case.

review_comments: We do not need `force_update` here as it enforces to  always write the state. Instead we extend the test to make sure that after expiry the state change is processed, even if the same value is received.

When a sensor has `expire_after` set, it will set `self._expired` to False. As long as the sensor is not expired, it will stay `False` and hence will not change. If the sensor expires, the state is always saved and `self._expired` is set to `True`. When a new value is received, the timer will be reset and `self._expired` will be set to `False` again.

When a `binary_sensor` has `expire_after` set, it will set `self._expired` to `False`. As long as the sensor is not expired, it will stay `False` and will not change. If the sensor expires, the state is always saved and `self._expired` is set to `True`. When a new value is received, the timer will be reset and `self._expired` will be set to `False` again.

We do not need `force_update` here as it enforces to  always write the state. Instead we extend the test to make sure that after expiry the state change is processed, even if the same value is received.
